name: Encoder-decoder vs decoder-only multimodal serving
arithmetic_intensity: Encoder-decoder architectures (Whisper, Flamingo) process the input modality in a separate encoder, then decode the output autoregressively. The encoder runs once per input, the decoder runs once per output token. Decoder-only with visual tokens (LLaVA, Pixtral, Qwen2-VL) processes the entire input (text + visual tokens) in one prefill pass, then decodes autoregressively. The serving implication is that encoder-decoder architectures have a fixed encoder cost per input, while decoder-only architectures have a prefill cost that scales with total input length (text + visual).
scales_with: input_resolution (encoder-decoder: linear in encoder cost; decoder-only: linear in prefill cost)
model_width (both: quadratic in MLP, linear in attention)
workarounds: Use encoder-decoder for speech-to-text (Whisper) - encoder cost is fixed per audio input
Use decoder-only for vision-language (LLaVA, Pixtral) - simpler serving, no separate encoder schedule
Use Perceiver/Q-Former to compress visual tokens in decoder-only - reduces prefill cost
Use encoder caching for repeated inputs (multi-turn chat)
notes: TWO ARCHITECTURE FAMILIES: (1) Encoder-decoder (Whisper, Flamingo): separate encoder and decoder. The encoder processes the input modality (audio, vision) once, producing a latent representation. The decoder generates output autoregressively, attending to the encoder output. Serving implication: encoder cost is fixed per input, decoder cost scales with output length. The encoder can be cached for repeated inputs. (2) Decoder-only with visual tokens (LLaVA, Pixtral, Qwen2-VL): the vision encoder produces visual tokens that are prepended to the text tokens. The entire sequence is processed in one prefill pass. Serving implication: prefill cost scales with total input length (text + visual), decode cost scales with output length. The vision encoder is a separate forward pass that can be cached. The key difference is that encoder-decoder architectures separate the input processing from the output generation, while decoder-only architectures fuse them. For serving, this means encoder-decoder architectures can cache the encoder output independently of the decoder, while decoder-only architectures must cache the entire prefill. Whisper is the canonical encoder-decoder for speech; LLaVA/Pixtral/Qwen2-VL are the canonical decoder-only for vision.
